clue.text: Ultimately, Kingsley Amis has claimed silly bloomer in plot?

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of these three words are jumbled into a new order
ultimately means at the end, so take only the last letter of the novelist's first name

explanation.surface: A tale about the novelist Kingsley Amis supposedly making a daft blunder somewhere in a novel's storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder to go with 'silly' and 'plot' looks like a storyline; in fact a bloomer is a flowering plant and the plot is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This autumn aster is a flower, a thing that blooms, which a gardener might grow in a bed or allotment.

clue.text: Phone in camper van?

parts.note: a mobile is a cellphone, as opposed to a landline
being in means being at home rather than away

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a phone has been left inside the camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone in' reads like a call to a radio show; split it into its two meanings instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A camper van is one example of a residence on wheels, hence the question mark marking a definition by example.

clue.text: Use nice room to relax official

indicators.note: to relax is to loosen up, so the letters of these three words are loosened and set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An instruction for a bureaucrat to unwind in a pleasant room.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal and following set procedure, so something official in manner is stately and formal in style.

clue.text: In Insta post, a sycophant's falseness?

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning several of them

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fawning flatterer's post on Instagram is insincere.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning one's faith or cause is a kind of disloyalty, being false to former beliefs.

clue.text: Turning up, ring on swallow recorded

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to ring is to dial a number on a phone
to swallow a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: Someone notes a phone ringing while a drink is downed, all captured on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians lay down a track when they record it in the studio, so the phrase means put on record.

clue.text: A snort from pig briefly close to piglet — bless!

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article a used before a vowel

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pig's grunt is written oink

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An affectionate exclamation over a pig's snort near its little piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bless!' reads like a cooing aside about the piglet, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate someone by smearing holy oil is a ritual act of blessing.

clue.text: Dishearten exile needing to support daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits below it, so the daughter's letter comes first

parts.note: to exile someone is to eject or expel them

explanation.surface: A banished parent dispirited at having to provide for a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to lower someone's spirits or make them downcast.

clue.text: Female singer lacks piano and something to write with

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Pink (often styled P!nk) is an American pop singer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A female vocalist has no piano but does have something to write with.
explanation.definitionFit: Pens are filled with this coloured fluid, which is what puts writing on the page.

clue.text: City's thick royal palms rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the concealed letters are read upwards, so backwards
to palm something is to conceal it in the hand, so these words conceal the letters

explanation.surface: A city boasts dense groves of regal palm trees growing tall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in northern England, famous for its Minster and medieval walls.

clue.text: Following pub party, short row over wine

indicators.note: following tells us the next pieces come after the pub and party pieces

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
a do is an informal party

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a line is a row, as of people or words
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: After a party at the pub, a quick argument breaks out over the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but means a line; 'over' reads as 'about' but is cricket's O.
explanation.definitionFit: A light red wine from the shores of Lake Garda in Italy.

clue.text: Card made by Josh and Rex

parts.note: to josh is to tease or joke
R is short for Rex, Latin for king, as in a monarch's signature

explanation.surface: A greetings card produced jointly by two friends called Josh and Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh and Rex look like names; one is a verb, the other the royal R.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a wag or comedian, someone who plays the fool; it is also the wild card in a pack.

clue.text: Confined in university, fibbed about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the fibbing word goes round the university

parts.note: to fib is to tell a small lie
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A student stuck at university tells lies about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the university, so the lying goes around MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricted within bounds, which is what being confined means.

clue.text: Steal extremely essential metal

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to steal a metal that is vitally needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery metallic element, chemical symbol Ni, also used in coins.

clue.text: Vigorous physical effort of turn introducing musical

indicators.note: introducing means coming before, so the bend precedes the show

parts.note: an elbow is a sharp bend or turn, as in a pipe or road
Grease is the stage and film musical set in a 1950s high school

explanation.surface: Describes the strenuous energy of a performer's turn that opens a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for hard manual work, especially scrubbing or polishing.

clue.text: Be enraged about drinking drop of rotgut here?

definitions.text: Be enraged about drinking drop of rotgut here?

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order
a drop is a tiny amount, so just the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Imagine getting furious over a sip of cheap liquor in a pub's outdoor area.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: an outdoor drinking area where one might sip rough booze and grow angry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor seating area attached to a pub, where drink, good or bad, is served.

clue.text: Tools Dawn has lost — spades

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have lost their way and come out scrambled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games such as bridge

explanation.surface: Dawn has mislaid some tools, including her spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' looks like more garden tools in the list, but it is the card suit's S.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws worked by one hand are woodworking implements, hence tools.

clue.text: An honour to hold ball for music producer

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the ball goes inside

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
O looks like a ball by its shape

explanation.surface: A record producer receives a royal honour at a gala ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music producer' suggests a person in a studio; it is a woodwind instrument that produces music.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument, so literally something that produces musical sound.

clue.text: US hotel uniform — it's seen in heaps

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside, so this little word goes within the other

parts.note: heaps means lots, or many

explanation.surface: An American hotel's staff uniform is spotted lying around in piles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' looks like the United States; read it as the pronoun 'us', meaning people at large.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind as a whole is all of us, the human race.

clue.text: Annoyed, run out to grab doctor's hat

indicators.note: to grab means to seize and hold, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: sore can mean irritated or annoyed
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: An irritated man dashes out to snatch back his GP's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' is the cricket dismissal, scored RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brimmed Mexican hat worn against the sun.

clue.text: Government ministry checking oxygen in atmosphere

indicators.note: checking means holding back or restraining, so the ministry holds the gas inside it

parts.note: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A government department monitoring oxygen levels in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The prevailing feeling or tone of a place or occasion, its ambience.

clue.text: Grow fat, initially undermining sporting contest

indicators.note: sporting can mean showing off or wearing in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so take just the first letter

explanation.surface: Putting on weight in the early stages ruins a sporting competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like a description of the contest; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-pulling trial of strength between two teams, a classic sports-day event.

clue.text: Note merchants essentially managed capital

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so take the central letter

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A note that traders essentially ran the financial capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Iran.

clue.text: First of all, indoor market's assistant wraps china animal

indicators.note: wraps means encloses, so the friend goes inside
first of all means the first letter of all of the next three words

parts.note: china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: An indoor market stallholder's helper packages a porcelain animal ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain; it is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), giving PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An African antelope known for its leaping, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Encounters European returning favour

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: A traveller meets a European who returns a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Favour in the sense of high regard or approval, as in held in high regard.

clue.text: Einstein possibly beginning to admire province in Canada

parts.note: Albert is Einstein's first name, possibly signalling one example of the name

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Perhaps Einstein began to admire a Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie province of western Canada, capital Edmonton.

clue.text: Gents' appearance discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a guise is an outward appearance or semblance

explanation.surface: Talk about the look of a men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents'' looks like a men's toilet; read it as men in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal plural for men or chaps, so a synonym for gentlemen.

clue.text: Meal starting late in part of Oxford?

indicators.note: starting late means the opening letter is missing, as if it arrived after the start

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A college dinner in Oxford begins behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city; it is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a laced shoe, and the top part of a shoe covering the foot is called its top piece.

clue.text: Prince's odd parts for Purple Rain perhaps

indicators.note: odd parts means the letters in odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth

explanation.surface: Prince's quirky contributions to his song Purple Rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purple Rain' reads as the song; it is also Prince's 1984 film, an example of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a film, of which Purple Rain is one example.

clue.text: Hair accessory I dab clean for a new style

indicators.note: a new style means a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone dabs a hairband clean so they can wear a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain hairband worn over the head, named after Alice in Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: Back a railway service going around fashion school

indicators.note: going around is used loosely here to show the service is combined with the fashion piece

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
mode means fashion or style
RN is the Royal Navy, known as the Senior Service

explanation.surface: Supporting a train service that runs round a fashion school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' promises a container, but the Navy simply follows the fashion word, so the phrase only joins them. The Royal Navy is nicknamed the Senior Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of British state secondary school for pupils who did not go to grammar school, mostly closed in the 1960s and 70s.
